title: Corrigendum to ‘‘Sampling protocol for the determination of nutrients and contaminants in fish and other seafood – The EAF-Nansen programme” [MethodsX 7 (2020) 101063]
author: Moxness Reksten, Bøkevoll, et al.
materials: Indicator PCBs (also called ICES-6 or PCB

Sample material was mixed with hydro matrix and internal standards were added (13C labelled EDF-8999 for PCDD/F, EC-5379 and EC-4937 for PCBs, EO-5100-10X, EO-5035, EO-5161, EO-5337, EO-5240, EO-5241, and EO-5003 for PBDEs (Cambridge Isotope Laboratories, Andover, MA, USA)). The analytes were extracted with hexane by an accelerated solvent extractor (ASE 350®, Dionex Corporation, Sunnyvale, CA, USA) under elevated pressure and temperature (100°C, 1500 psi) and concentrated using Turbovap II (Zymark/discontinued, Caliper Life Sciences, Mountain View, CA, USA). The sample extracts were purified using high performance clean-up columns (silver nitrate-, sulfuric acid/silica-, carbon- and alumina column), on an automated GO-6HT system (DSP-Systems, Ede, Netherlands). PBDEs, ndl-PCBs, and mono-ortho-PCBs were collected in one fraction, whereas PCDD/Fs and non-ortho PCBs were collected in a second fraction. Furthermore, solvent exchange and adding of recovery standards (S-5117-ASS-NN and S-5118-ASS-NN, Chiron, Trondheim, Norway) were executed by automated liquid handling (Microlab Starlet, Hamilton Nordic AB, Kista, Sweden).

PCDD/F and non-ortho-PCB analysis was performed by high-resolution gas chromatography/high resolution mass spectrometry (HRGC-HRMS) (HRGC, Trace 2000 series; HRMS, DFS, ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA), equipped with a fused silica capillary column (30 m x 0.25 mm I.D. and 0.25 µm film thickness, Rxi-5SIL MS, Restek, Bellefonte, USA).

Octa-deka PBDEs were analysed by negative chemical ionisation GC/MS (GC, Trace 1310; MS, DSQ, ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA), equipped with a fused silica capillary column (15 m x 0.25 mm I.D. and 0.1 µm film thickness, RTX-1614, Restek, Bellefonte, USA).

steps.title: Define target analytes
steps.instruction: Identify the 17 PCDD/F congeners (2,3,7,8‑TCDD; 1,2,3,7,8‑PeCDD; 1,2,3,4,7,8‑HxCDD; 1,2,3,6,7,8‑HxCDD; 1,2,3,7,8,9‑HxCDD; 1,2,3,4,6,7,8‑HpCDD; OCDD; 2,3,7,8‑TCDF; 1,2,3,7,8‑PeCDF; 2,3,4,7,8‑PeCDF; 1,2,3,4,7,8‑HxCDF; 1,2,3,6,7,8‑HxCDF; 1,2,3,7,8,9‑HxCDF; 2,3,4,6,7,8‑HxCDF; 1,2,3,4,6,7,8‑HpCDF; 1,2,3,4,7,8,9‑HpCDF; OCDF), the dioxin‑like PCBs (non‑ortho: CB 77, 81, 126, 169; mono‑ortho: CB 105, 114, 118, 123, 156, 157, 167, 189), the indicator PCBs (ICES‑6: CB 28, 52, 101, 138, 153, 180; plus extra non‑dioxin‑like PCB 31 from 2020), and the PBDEs (tri‑hepta: BDE 28, 47, 49, 66, 99, 100, 119, 138, 153, 154, 183; tri‑hepta added from 2020: BDE 35, 71, 75, 85, 118; octa‑deka added from 2020: BDE 196, 197, 206, 207, 209).

steps.title: Prepare sample with matrix and standards
steps.instruction: Mix the sample material with hydro matrix and add the following 13C‑labelled internal standards: EDF‑8999 for PCDD/F, EC‑5379 and EC‑4937 for PCBs, and EO‑5100‑10X, EO‑5035, EO‑5161, EO‑5337, EO‑5240, EO‑5241, EO‑5003 for PBDEs (Cambridge Isotope Laboratories, Andover, MA, USA).

steps.title: Extract analytes with ASE
steps.instruction: Extract the spiked sample with hexane using an accelerated solvent extractor (ASE 350®, Dionex Corp.) at 100 °C and 1500 psi.

steps.title: Concentrate extracts
steps.instruction: Concentrate the ASE extracts with a Turbovap II (Zymark/Caliper Life Sciences, Mountain View, CA, USA).

steps.title: Purify extracts and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Pass the concentrated extract through high‑performance clean‑up columns (silver nitrate, sulfuric‑acid/silica, carbon, and alumina) on an automated GO‑6HT system (DSP‑Systems, Ede, Netherlands). Collect PBDEs, ndl‑PCBs and mono‑ortho‑PCBs in one fraction and PCDD/Fs together with non‑ortho PCBs in a second fraction.

steps.title: Solvent exchange and add recovery standards
steps.instruction: Perform solvent exchange and add the recovery standards S‑5117‑ASS‑NN and S‑5118‑ASS‑NN (Chiron, Trondheim, Norway) using an automated liquid‑handling robot (Microlab Starlet, Hamilton Nordic AB, Kista, Sweden).

steps.title: Analyze PCDD/Fs and non‑ortho PCBs by HRGC‑HRMS
steps.instruction: Inject the PCDD/F and non‑ortho PCB fraction into a high‑resolution gas chromatograph (Trace 2000 series, ThermoFisher Scientific) coupled to a high‑resolution mass spectrometer (DFS, ThermoFisher). Use a fused‑silica capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm I.D., 0.25 µm film, Rxi‑5SIL MS, Restek, Bellefonte, USA).

steps.title: Analyze ndl‑PCBs, mono‑ortho PCBs, tri‑hepta PBDEs by GC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Inject the ndl‑PCB, mono‑ortho PCB and tri‑hepta PBDE fraction into a GC‑MS/MS system (GC 7890A; MS/MS 7000B/C, Agilent Technologies) equipped with a low‑bleed proprietary phased column (30 m × 0.25 mm I.D., 0.25 µm film, Agilent J&W, Santa Clara, CA, USA).

steps.title: Analyze octa‑deka PBDEs by NCI GC/MS
steps.instruction: Inject the octa‑deka PBDE fraction into a negative‑chemical‑ionisation GC/MS (GC Trace 1310; MS DSQ, ThermoFisher Scientific) using a fused‑silica capillary column (15 m × 0.25 mm I.D., 0.1 µm film, RTX‑1614, Restek, Bellefonte, USA).

steps.title: Quantify congeners using isotope‑dilution calibration
steps.instruction: Quantify all congeners by isotope‑dilution/internal‑standard method using relative response factors (RRs) or response factors (RFs) from calibration curves. Use a five‑point calibration curve for PCDD/Fs and non‑ortho PCBs (US EPA 1613 and 1668 methods). Use eight‑point calibration curves for mono‑ortho PCBs, ndl‑PCBs and tri‑hepta PBDEs. Use five‑point calibration curves weighted 1/S² for octa‑deka PBDEs.

steps.title: Report results as WHO‑TEQ per wet weight
steps.instruction: Express final quantified PCDD/F and DL‑PCB values as pg WHO‑TEQ / g wet weight using the 2005 WHO‑TEFs (EU legislation EC 2011). Report concentrations below the limit of quantification (LOQ) as the LOQ (upper‑bound) to avoid underestimation of risk.
